MAJOR: Scan calls `store.Head` for every manifest entry although `List` already returns the same `ObjectInfo` (Size/Checksum): O(N) extra round trips, rate-limit and runtime risk on large enterprise manifests.

Any `Head` error is reported as `Missing`; transient/permission failures are indistinguishable from true absence, producing false drift that can trigger needless repairs. Must branch on a typed NotFound.

`LifecycleCapable` has no version parameter, yet S3 object lock is per object version and the store already tracks `Version`; retention/legal-hold can only be read/applied for "latest" — an auditability gap for versioned, legally-held objects.

The diff sets `Capabilities{ObjectLock: true}` and reads `Capabilities().ObjectLock`, but never introduces the `ObjectLock` field; if it is not already present in the shown file, this does not compile — the "go build/test PASS" claim needs proof.
New modules `objpolicy` / `objreconcile` arrive with no `go.work`, CI, Makefile or lint wiring, and no `go.sum`; absent wiring they will never be built, vetted or tested in pipeline.

Local `Put` silently accepts `Immutable: true` with no retention: the caller believes immutability is enforced while nothing is locked. Fail closed or at minimum emit an explicit rejection, consistent with the retention path.
MINOR: S3 `PutOptions` retention is hardcoded to GOVERNANCE with no COMPLIANCE path at put time; document the limitation or extend the option.

`cleanPath`'s `strings.Contains(c, "..")` is dead code (`path.Clean` already resolves ".."); the traversal test passes only because Clean rewrites the path, giving false confidence in a check that never fires.
`Mint` silently rewrites the caller's key via `cleanPath` before signing, so a URL can be minted for a different object than requested; prefer rejecting non-canonical keys.
Checksum comparison assumes bare hex sha256 on both sides with no algorithm-prefix normalization (`sha256:...` vs raw hex) → whole-manifest false mismatches if formats differ.
`Scan` prefix guard is a raw `strings.HasPrefix`, so prefix "p" (no trailing slash) makes "pother/..." valid; normalize prefix as `objpolicy` does.
`ObjectLifecycle` calls `GetBucketVersioning` on every invocation; cache it per store instance.
Two divergent ObjectStore test fakes (`stubStore`, `fakeStore`) plus separate local/S3 lifecycle tests instead of one reusable conformance suite.
NIT: Stdlib `log.Printf` with concatenated deny reasons instead of the repo's structured logger; reasons should be fields, not string fragments.
No boundary tests for TTL exactly at 30s and 15m, only out-of-range cases.
`Report.Invalid` conflates duplicate and out-of-prefix entries with no reason code, forcing re-parsing to act.
Signed PUT/DELETE URLs are mintable based only on a caller-supplied method string; consider gating by caller role/scope.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-scoped foundation: typed `ErrUnsupported`, a central privilege boundary for signed URLs, a read-only deterministic reconciler, and fail-closed local behavior — the shape is right.

Top risks: reconciliation correctness (Head errors → false "missing", N+1 Head) and lifecycle integrity (no version-scoped retention/legal hold), plus unproven build wiring for the two new modules and the possibly-missing `Capabilities.ObjectLock` field.
Address the MAJOR items before merge; nothing here blocks the overall direction.
